text:
The examination process can be summarised as follows. The process starts
when the female patient is examined by an outpatient physician, who decides
whether she is healthy or needs to undertake an additional examination. In the
former case, the physician fills out the examination form and the patient can
leave. In the latter case, an examination and follow-up treatment order is placed
by the physician who additionally fills out a request form. Beyond information
about the patient, the request form includes details about the examination 
requested and refers to a suitable lab. Furthermore, the outpatient physician
informs the patient about potential risks. If the patient signs an informed consent
and agrees to continue with the procedure, a delegate of the physician
arranges an appointment of the patient with one of the wards. The latter is
then responsible for taking a sample to be analysed in the lab later. Before the
appointment, the required examination and sampling is prepared by a nurse of
the ward based on the information provided by the outpatient section. Then, a
ward physician takes the sample requested. He further sends it to the lab indicated
in the request form and conducts the follow-up treatment of the patient.
After receiving the sample, a physician of the lab validates its state and decides
whether the sample can be used for analysis or whether it is contaminated and
a new sample is required. After the analysis is performed by a medical technical
assistant of the lab, a lab physician validates the results. Finally, a physician
from the outpatient department makes the diagnosis and prescribes the therapy
for the patient.

verdict.justification: No gap found, but 5 requirement(s) from the text could not be associated with any clear activity in the observed process -- neither confirmed nor refuted. This verdict is NOT a confirmation of full faithfulness.
verdict.scope: This verdict covers the causal reachability of the requirements expressed in the source text, not the general quality of the process model -- a multiplicity defect (an activity executed more than once due to a mismatched branching structure) is not covered by this verdict, even if the process is otherwise well-formed.

non_verifiable.quote: The process starts when the female patient is examined by an outpatient physician, who decides whether she is healthy or needs to undertake an additional examination.
non_verifiable.explanation:
The process requires that the patient be healthy before the activity "patient healthy" can occur. However, the observed process does not clearly show any step where this condition is checked or confirmed.

The source text states: "The process starts when the female patient is examined by an outpatient physician, who decides whether she is healthy or needs to undertake an additional examination."

Since no matching activity is found in the process, it is impossible to confirm whether this requirement is met. (This same root cause also affects: examination form filled out.)

non_verifiable.quote: Furthermore, the outpatient physician informs the patient about potential risks.
non_verifiable.explanation: The process requires that the "request form filled out" must happen before the "patient informed" activity, but the observed process does not show this step clearly. The source text states: "Furthermore, the outpatient physician informs the patient about potential risks." Since we cannot see whether the form was filled out before the patient was informed, we cannot confirm if this requirement was met. (This same root cause also affects: Make appointment, Perform follow-up treatment, Prepare examination, Take sample, informed consent signed, patient appointed, patient consented, patient sampled, request form filled out, request form includes details, request form refers to lab.)

non_verifiable.quote: He further sends it to the lab indicated in the request form and conducts the follow-up treatment of the patient.
non_verifiable.explanation:
The activity "Perform follow-up treatment" requires that the patient's sample is not contaminated. However, the process does not clearly show when or how this absence of contamination is checked, making it impossible to confirm whether this condition is met or not.

The source text states: *"He further sends it to the lab indicated in the request form and conducts the follow-up treatment of the patient."* This shows that a condition exists before follow-up treatment, but it does not explain how contamination is verified. (This same root cause also affects: sample contaminated.)

non_verifiable.quote: Finally, a physician from the outpatient department makes the diagnosis and prescribes the therapy for the patient.
non_verifiable.explanation: The activity "patient diagnosed" requires a prior condition, as stated in the source text: "Finally, a physician from the outpatient department makes the diagnosis and prescribes the therapy for the patient." However, the observed process does not clearly show what must happen before this step, so we cannot confirm whether this requirement is met or not. (This same root cause also affects: patient under therapy.)

non_verifiable.quote: After the analysis is performed by a medical technical assistant of the lab, a lab physician validates the results.
non_verifiable.explanation: The activity "Analyse sample" requires that an analysis has already been performed, as stated in the source text: "After the analysis is performed by a medical technical assistant of the lab, a lab physician validates the results." However, the observed process does not clearly show which activity corresponds to this required analysis, making it impossible to check whether this condition is met. (This same root cause also affects: analysis performed.)
